root.note: Clouds cover the sun. Etymonline and Wiktionary link sky to a root meaning ‘to cover, to hide’; Old English scūa ‘shadow’ and scēo ‘cloud’ are probably related.

stages.meaning: the space above us where we see the sun and clouds

history: Sky is another word from the Vikings. In Old Norse, ský meant ‘cloud’, and in early Middle English sky also meant ‘a cloud’. The space above us was called heaven (Old English heofon). From about 1300, sky slowly took over the meaning ‘the space above the earth’, and heaven was used more and more for the home of God. English took many simple words like this from Old Norse, among them egg, knife, window and even they. The word probably goes back to a root meaning ‘to cover’: clouds cover the sun. In Danish and Norwegian, sky still means ‘cloud’ today.
historyEinfach: Sky is a Viking word. In the Viking language, ský meant ‘cloud’. At first, sky meant ‘cloud’ in English too. The old English word for the sky was heaven. Later, sky became the word for the blue space above us. Heaven became the home of God. In Danish and Norwegian, sky still means ‘cloud’.

elsewhere.text: Danish and Norwegian sky looks like the English word, but it means ‘cloud’, just like the Old Norse word that English borrowed. The Danish word for the sky is himmel.
